Can’t book a flight or secure an appointment at her overseas outposts? Bartov’s skin-care sets are also available online for anyone to achieve her red carpet-ready glow from home.

Ahead, Bartov shares what she can’t live without (including her most priceless essentials), the ingredients and devices that have piqued her interest and those that she recommends skipping.

In a nutshell, what led you to becoming a star-trusted skin expert?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, keren bartov: ever since i was a little girl, i’ve been drawn to everything related to beauty, aesthetics and skin care. Very quickly, I discovered there was so much more to it than I had imagined. It was always something I loved, but as I got older, I realized I also wanted a stable career, something I could build and grow over time, so I decided to study cosmetology. I fell in love with the field, started studying and exploring it in depth and realized I had found my place.

Today, I feel like I’ve somehow managed to bring all the worlds I love together: beauty, aesthetics, creativity, working with people and even a little bit of the entertainment world, especially when I’m preparing actresses and models for some of their biggest moments.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for more than 17 years, i’ve been studying, researching and exploring advanced technologies and treatment methods from around the world. What started as genuine curiosity and passion eventually became the treatment method I’ve developed over the years.

Sebagaimana diketahui, developing my own skin-care line was a natural extension of that journey. I wanted to take the knowledge and experience I’d gained in the treatment room and translate it into products that could become part of my clients’ everyday routines. To this day, nothing excites me more than seeing how the right treatment and skin-care routine can transform not only someone’s skin, but also their confidence.

How do you decide what new product or technology makes the cut? What are the red flags that tell you something is just a fad?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i never introduce a technology or ingredient simply because it’s new or everyone is talking about it. For me, innovation has to be backed by science, safety and meaningful results.

Before incorporating a new device or product, I look at the research behind it, how it works, whether it’s suitable for different skin types and how it can complement the treatments and products I already use.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i take exactly the same approach when developing my own skin care. Every formula needs to have a clear purpose. For example, with Melanin Correcting Serum, the focus is on addressing the appearance of uneven pigmentation, while Hydra Reboost Cream is about providing the hydration and comfort the skin needs. What ingredients, devices, or innovations are exciting you most right now, and why?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, one technology i’m particularly excited about is onda pro, which uses targeted microwave energy to address concerns including skin firmness and the appearance of facial contours. What interests me most is how I can incorporate it into a broader, personalized treatment protocol.

Berdasarkan laporan, another is xerf, a radiofrequency technology designed for non-invasive skin tightening. Diungkapkan bahwa when it comes to ingredients, i’m a strong believer in peptides, active acids, and ingredients supported by solid clinical research. I’m not interested in whatever ingredient happens to be trending online. I’m interested in what can genuinely address a specific skin concern.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, peptides are particularly interesting to me, which is why i love incorporating a peptide serum into a targeted skin-care routine. I’m also a big believer in exfoliating acids when they’re used correctly. Diungkapkan bahwa to me, real innovation isn’t always about discovering something entirely new. It’s about finding smarter, more precise ways to use ingredients and technologies that have already proven themselves.

What beauty trends do you suggest clients skip?.

I’m not a big fan of beauty gimmicks that look amazing on social media but don’t necessarily deliver meaningful, long-term results.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, sheet masks and under-eye patches are good examples. They can provide a temporary boost of hydration or make the skin feel refreshed, but I don’t see them as a substitute for skin care that genuinely works on the skin.

Diungkapkan bahwa i’d much rather see someone invest in a well-formulated serum that addresses their actual skin concerns. That’s why I’ve always placed so much emphasis on active formulas, whether it’s Advanced Skin Serum as part of a consistent routine or Melanin Correcting Serum for someone looking to address uneven skin tone.

Diungkapkan bahwa i’m also cautious about trends like at-home microneedling. It’s a procedure that requires professional knowledge, and when done incorrectly, it can cause irritation, infection and damage to the skin. Another trend I’m not a fan of is using active acids without understanding their concentrations, how they interact, or whether they’re suitable for your skin.

Berdasarkan laporan, i absolutely believe in advanced skin care and using multiple products, but every product should have a purpose. For me, the question isn’t how good a product looks on camera. I don’t believe in adding something to your routine just because it’s gone viral. It’s what it actually does for your skin.

Sebagaimana diketahui, walk us through your treatments. What do you consider when creating custom protocols for clients?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, no two people have exactly the same skin, so no two treatments should ever be identical. I start with a thorough skin assessment, looking at texture, hydration levels, pigmentation, elasticity and sensitivity. I also consider age, lifestyle, skin-care habits, previous treatments and, of course, what the client wants to achieve.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, one of the things that makes my method different is the ability to address several concerns within a single treatment. But personalization doesn’t end when the client leaves the clinic. For example, I might combine technologies targeting firmness, texture, hydration, and radiance, carefully selecting devices that complement one another. I also look at what they’re using at home, because professional treatments and daily skin care should support one another.

Berdasarkan laporan, someone dealing with pigmentation might benefit from incorporating melanin correcting serum into their routine, while someone whose skin needs more hydration might be better suited to hydra reboost cream. In other cases, I might focus on introducing active serums gradually or adjusting the evening routine.

Diungkapkan bahwa i don’t believe in a one-size-fits-all facial or a one-size-fits-all skin-care routine. I believe in understanding exactly what the skin needs and building the right protocol around it.

What are your top tips for a solid foundational skin-care routine? What people avoid?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i’m a big believer in a comprehensive skin-care routine that incorporates multiple products and active ingredients, as long as they’re carefully selected and work well together. I don’t think we should be afraid of having several steps. What’s important is understanding what each product does and why it’s there.

For me, the foundation of great skin is proper cleansing, targeted active ingredients, hydration, and daily sun protection.

Berdasarkan laporan, in the evening, i always recommend starting with a double cleanse. I use my Micellar Water to remove makeup and impurities, followed by a gentle milky cleanser to thoroughly cleanse the skin.

Berdasarkan laporan, once the skin is clean, i like to work with different serums depending on its needs. Booster Peel & Glow Serum is one of my favorites for improving the appearance of skin texture and radiance, while Advanced Skin Serum is an essential part of my own routine.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for clients dealing with uneven skin tone and pigmentation, i often recommend melanin correcting serum. I also love incorporating a peptide serum, as peptides are among the ingredients I believe in for supporting firmer, healthier-looking skin.

Diungkapkan bahwa i place enormous importance on nighttime skin care. While we sleep, the skin goes through natural renewal and repair processes, and I love using those hours to give it targeted care.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one ingredient i believe in most is retinol. It’s one of the most extensively researched ingredients in skin care, with well-established benefits for improving skin texture, the appearance of fine lines, and uneven skin tone over time.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that belief was also behind the development of next gen, my retinol-infused night cream. I consider it an important part of a targeted evening routine, with the frequency of use adjusted to the individual’s skin.

Diungkapkan bahwa hydration is equally important. I love Hydra Reboost Cream for keeping the skin feeling comfortable and moisturized, and Hydration Glow Spray is one of my favorite finishing touches for an instant boost of freshness and radiance. It’s also a product I love having with me when I travel.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in the morning, my focus is on hydration, protection and maintaining healthy-looking skin. Sunscreen is absolutely non-negotiable.

Diungkapkan bahwa of course, not every active ingredient is suitable for everyone, and i don’t recommend layering strong acids and retinol indiscriminately. It’s important to tailor combinations and frequency of use to the skin’s needs and tolerance.

What should we avoid? Constantly switching products, combining active ingredients without understanding how they work together and expecting overnight results.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i always compare skin care to going to the gym. If you want to see real results, you have to be consistent. It’s the combination of the right products, a consistent routine and professional treatments that makes the difference.

What are some essentials that you can’t live without right now?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if there’s one skin-care product i can’t live without, it’s my advanced skin serum. It’s one of the products I reach for every single day and a true essential in my routine. I love how it helps my skin look smoother, fresher and more radiant. No matter where I’m traveling, it always comes with me.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i’m a big believer in movement and taking care of my body. Strength training is an important part of my routine, and I also love going for walks. With all the traveling and work, it’s my time to clear my head and focus on myself.

Berdasarkan laporan, i love activewear that’s comfortable enough for a workout but stylish enough to wear outside the gym. Alo Yoga’s Airlift leggings are exactly my style, especially on days when I’m going straight from a workout to meetings or errands.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i absolutely love victoria beckham’s tailoring. There’s something so precise, feminine and effortlessly elegant about her designs. A beautifully tailored blazer and trousers are a combination I can always rely on, especially for meetings and events.

Berdasarkan laporan, i love this bag. There’s something iconic and timeless about it, and I’ve always preferred pieces that never go out of style.

Diungkapkan bahwa for me, great foundation should still let your skin look like skin. I love a lightweight base that evens out the complexion, adds freshness and lets the skin’s natural texture show through. That’s exactly the kind of makeup I gravitate toward.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i love makeup that adds a subtle touch of light without looking heavy. This is one of those products that can instantly bring a little color and radiance to the face, especially when I’m going straight from a long workday to dinner or an event.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i love candles and beautiful home fragrances, and diptyque is one of my favorite brands. Baies has that elegant, comforting scent that instantly creates a lovely atmosphere at home. Lighting a candle at the end of the day is one of my little rituals.

And one thing I could never leave off the list: Evenings at Home With My Husband and Kids.

Diungkapkan bahwa this might not be a product, but it’s the one thing i truly can’t live without. I spend so much time traveling and working around the world that the simplest moments at home mean the most to me. Family dinners, spending time with my kids or just having a quiet evening with my husband are the moments I look forward to most.

Related Stories ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Has 10 Credited Writers, Including Hugh Jackman and Ryan Reynolds Brad Pitt to Star in ‘Connector’ from ‘Sound of Metal’ Director Darius Marder for Apple.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the 15-minute short film stars rising young actress martha malone as fay, alongside clare dunne as mam and tim creed as dad. When we first meet Fay, she’s launched a silent protest, announcing to her mother (via a titular paper plane message) that she will not return to their home until her father, who we instantly understand is a toxic presence, leaves for good. As Fay and her trusty dog sit it out in a grassy lot across the street from the family home, Ronan’s film unfolds with grace and honesty, ending on a heart-stopping note.

Diungkapkan bahwa ronan also gathered an impressive roster behind the camera, including producer shirin eren, who previously produced ronan’s “the outrun,” ifta-winning editor nathan nugent, and kate mccullough, all of whom she describes in sparkling terms. You can get a taste of the film’s tone, visual style, and wonderful performances in an exclusive clip below.

Ahead, Ronan goes deep on her process, why she felt the need to make the jump to directing now (thanks to her “Little Women” co-star Eliza Scanlen), emulating her favorite collaborators like Greta Gerwig and Joe Wright, the one thing about directing that really surprised her, and if she’s ready to make the jump to directing features.

The following interview has been edited and condensed for clarity and length.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, indiewire: when we spoke in 2024 for “the outrun,” you told me that you had wanted to direct since you were a child. Why was this the right project and the right moment?.

Diungkapkan bahwa saoirse ronan: i think it was a number of things. I was definitely starting to move into the next stage of adulthood. It was where I was at in my personal life. It felt like a shift was taking place for me internally. I was married, becoming a parent. Change was on the horizon.

Sebagaimana diketahui, and i think it felt, to be honest, if i don’t do it now, who knows when i’ll do it. I also wonder how many mothers in particular feel that way before they go into that next stage of their life where they’re like, “Actually, this is all quite unknown, and I don’t know if I don’t do it now, will it be another 10 years before I can find the time or the space within myself to do something like that that’s for me?” So it really gave me a lot of motivation being in that place personally.

Berdasarkan laporan, it’s something that i’ve always wanted to do. It just felt very serendipitous that it happened when it did. I guess I was ready to put that into action, and it was always going to be something that involved a young person and a mother, probably. I was always drawn toward directing, even from before I became an actor. And I’ve been so hugely influenced by the directors I’ve worked with since the age of 10. So felt like everything was aligning at that point.

Diungkapkan bahwa you also wrote this script. What was your writing process like? What surprised you about that?.

Berdasarkan laporan, maybe it’s different with journalism, although i’m sure it must be incredibly difficult in other ways, but writing’s just really hard. As the Italians say, piano, piano, little by little, you take a step forward, and you take two steps back. And I knew it would be, but to conjure up something out of nothing supposedly is mind-boggling. I guess I didn’t realize how much of it is about process. I’d never been in that position creatively and professionally where it was all on me, so to find the discipline to do that, sit down, and to go, “OK, well, it’s not going to happen if I don’t make it happen,” was a new challenge for me.

Berdasarkan laporan, i was so lucky to have shirin eren, my producer and my partner, jack [lowden], and lots of close friends who had already taken that step. Brilliant actor Eliza Scanlen, who’s already done three shorts, and she’s so much younger than I am, has actually been a huge inspiration to me. And I just thought, well, Jesus, if Eliza’s doing it, I have no excuse.

Berdasarkan laporan, what i’ve learned is, when it comes to doing a feature, i’d definitely love to work with a writer, because i’m not one, and i think there’s a lot i have to learn. This was incredibly personal, so it was coming from such a pure place that it had to come from me, and it had to be written by me. But I certainly am excited by the challenge of working with someone who actually does it for a living and to learn about how to structure something and add art and things like that.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in the film’s press notes, it says that this is “a love letter to your younger self. ” What was the most important thing that had to be in there for you, in terms of the script or the visuals or the casting?.

Diungkapkan bahwa there were two things that were very important to me. One was, tonally, I kept circling back to the magical realism route. I wanted it only ever to feel like we were seeing this through a child’s eyes, and in the way that a child makes sense out of the nonsensical and the seemingly impossible and the incredibly difficult thing to fathom and to swallow and to digest and to overcome. Creativity and imagination always plays a part for a child and just making sense out of anything in the world from day dot, from the moment that they’re here. I didn’t want it to feel like a fantasy, but I wanted it to feel like it was heightened in some way, hence the addition of the paper planes, which was something I used to do with my mom.

Diungkapkan bahwa i used to send her little paper planes when she’d send me to my room with a little note saying, “i’m really sorry that i did this. Please don’t send me back,” or whatever. Please don’t hate me. And I’d peek around the corner of whatever room she was in, I’d throw it at her, and then I’d run back to my room knowing logically she’d know it was me, but tricking myself into believing that she’d believed that this had seemingly come out of nowhere.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it was also very important to me that the father role was never vilified. I didn’t want this to be a piece that was overly black and white and critical when it comes to the situation. I didn’t want to just point the blame at one character. Although there’s clearly something very toxic and dark within the home that’s happening, and it’s ultimately being created by one member of the family for the most part, there’s a reason why this person unfortunately feels the need within themselves to create that toxicity.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i never wanted it to feel like there was any hatred or anger toward that character. You can say that we become more sophisticated, but I actually don’t know how much we do. Becoming a mother, I really felt with myself that you don’t ever stop being a child. It needed to very much be focused on the love of these two girls. And I think to have a character that’s an older female, an older person, and someone who’s younger, but who essentially both remind each other of their inner child, I wanted to bring that out too.

Berdasarkan laporan, you’ve worked with so many incredible filmmakers over the course of your career. Was there any filmmaker you really wanted to emulate in terms of how you ran your set?.

Diungkapkan bahwa oh gosh, how i ran my set! it’s a combination of a few people. The way he was on the ground with his crew, the clarity that he had at the top of the day, the structure he had when it came to planning, I’ve always responded really well to that. They’re not documentaries, so there needs to be this heightened quality to it. The fact that he and Peter Jackson as well always played music live on set, I’ve always felt like that’s a really helpful way to remind cast and crew that, yes, there’s emotional truth in this, but for me, I want to make movies, I want to make films. I think I was really influenced by that from working with him so early on. I think back in the day, the way Joe Wright ran his set was fantastic. I feel like having music on set can remind people of that and just get everyone on the same rhythm.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i think the way greta [gerwig] is just greta and john crowley, the way they are as directors with their actors, i haven’t marched with anyone greater than those two. One thing that Greta said is that you need to think of yourself as the most supportive audience member for your actors. They bring out something that I haven’t experienced with anyone else, really, and I’ll always strive to be a tenth to what they are as a director. She always makes you feel so loved and interesting and wanted, and so I wanted the actors to feel that way.

Diungkapkan bahwa and to be honest, weirdly, out of every kind of hat that i had to wear as director, directing the actors was the thing that made me the most nervous. I can’t steer them wrong. Everything else, I was all right, but it felt really natural. But to actually be in the driving seat with other actors and to guide them, I was really, really nervous about that and constantly feeling like, God, I can’t let them down. I always want them to feel safe, and they can do whatever they want to do.

Was that the most surprising thing for you?.

Berdasarkan laporan, yes, that really did surprise me. Well, sometimes it is actually, maybe that’s not true, but I haven’t been that kind of actor. I wasn’t expecting that, but actually when I think about it and when I think about the kind of actor that I am, it does make sense, because I’m not one of those actors ever that’s like, “Don’t worry, I’ll take control of the room. So that definitely took me by surprise just how self-conscious I was initially. But I think they were happy. ” Maybe I’ve started to do that more as I’ve gotten older, but we all know plenty of actors that will start giving other actors notes, which is never helpful. The girls said that they felt good, so that’s all I can ask for really.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in our interview for “the outrun,” we talked about process, and your process is so internal and personal. It’s about being in the moment. You’re not Method. You don’t get caught up in stuff, so I did wonder how that would translate to directing.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it was funny actually because that seemed to translate well. I feel like I know how to do that. I think because of the way I work, it’s so much about working with the crew and enjoying the atmosphere on set, and it feels so natural for me to be there, so I felt really confident doing that. I’ve been on so many sets where I’ve looked at directors or producers who don’t quite know how to talk to their crew, don’t quite know what the crew needs, and how to wrangle the truth, how to make them feel appreciated and motivated. I’ve been on so many sets and grown up with it, and more than anyone else, I spend time with the crew, and I hear what irks them, what their complaints are, what drives them forward, what they appreciate from a director, from a leader.

I loved working on the schedule with her. I loved working with my first AD. I don’t think being a director is necessarily the hardest job out of every crew member. I think that the skill of being a director is to surround yourself with really, really, really brilliant people who know what they’re doing and to have good taste.

It sounds like it was pretty joyous for you to assemble your crew.

I think what every director will tell you, which I now know, is that making a short film is fucking really hard and frustrating, because crew need to go and work on a film that will actually pay the money and will keep them employed for two, three months, and a short film is not going to do that.

Berdasarkan laporan, so actually being able to get the crew that you want can be really, really difficult, but it does mean that the people who do come on board are there because they really want to be. Berdasarkan laporan, you’re someone who started acting at a young age, so i find it very interesting and compelling that you centered your film around a young star. How did you make sure Martha felt safe and comfortable and supported?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i knew that on day one, martha was going to be super nervous. She was 14, 15 at the time, and she’d done a few things, but I think whenever any of us have our first day on set, no matter how experienced we are, we’re always scared. I just wanted her to know that I was too, that I was nervous as well, and that we were going to be nervous together, and it was OK, and we were going to take care of each other.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i have the utmost respect for young performers, and i think that when you find ones that are disciplined as well as being talented, you just need to make them feel like they’re never pressured, they’re supported, but they’re being pushed. You’re not necessarily wrapping them in cotton wool, but you want them to feel loved. I wanted her and Claire to feel loved and wanted because they were, and that ultimately I would have to guide us because somebody does, but that there was a contribution they were going to be able to make as performers that I couldn’t, and I valued that.

Berdasarkan laporan, you mentioned if you make a feature, you want to work with another writer. The inevitable question: Do you want to direct a feature?.

Diungkapkan bahwa yeah, i do. I do want to do a feature, and I think part of the reason why I was making shorts is because I wanted to see if I could, and if I could, then what was my style, and what did I respond to, and what did I need to work on, and what were my strengths, so that I didn’t use everyone as my training ground on a feature film.

Diungkapkan bahwa again, i’ve been on the other side of that as well, where you’ve got someone in the driving seat, and you’re like, “uh-oh. I didn’t want to put myself in that position. I really want to keep going with it. ” I didn’t want to put anyone else in that position. I loved it so much, and I do have a lot to learn. So I would love to do a feature. #76. ‘Heartland’ Review: Jessica Chastain Rocks a Stetson and a Swagger for a Soapy Nashville Noir

📅 13 Nov 2026

‘Heartland’ Review: Jessica Chastain Rocks a Stetson and a Swagger for a Soapy Nashville Noir

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://variety.com/2026/film/news/heartland-review-jessica-chastain-1236946587/

When a young relative goes missing, a jaded former country star returns to the industry that chewed her up in 'Country Strong' director Shana Feste's thriller, which can be gaudy fun, but eventually peters out.

Berdasarkan laporan, misty jones keeps her grammy in the fridge, alongside a near-empty tupperware of chicken broth and, well, not a whole lot else: a former country superstar turned burnt-out rural hermit, she more or less lives off what once was, but her memories don’t exactly nourish her. Peculiar details like these enliven “Heartland,” a missing-person mystery that returns writer-director Shana Feste to the Nashville milieu of her 2010 sophomore feature “Country Strong. ” So does Jessica Chastain‘s surprisingly brash, beery performance as Misty, whose no-bullshit demeanor serves her well when she must turn amateur detective, investigating the disappearance of a relative who happens to be a rising country star herself. Related Stories 'Ramayana,' 'Fatherland,' 'Dhurandhar' Lead International Film Festival of India Lineup Featuring Almodovar, Kore-eda, Kurosawa 'Gatto' Trailer: A Mobster Cat Is on His Last Life in Pixar's New Animated Movie.

Berdasarkan laporan, fusing southern-fried noir atmospherics with the sequinned kitsch of a music city backstage melodrama, “heartland” often hits the same undemanding guilty-pleasure groove as “country strong” — or indeed the six-season run of tv’s “nashville” in the 2010s. Feste’s thin screenplay is heavily reliant on Chastain’s brio to sustain a quest that only narrowly makes sense on a moment-to-moment basis, and never gathers much intrigue — since the villains are all glaringly identifiable as such from the get-go, while Misty’s rough-diamond integrity is never in doubt. What it isn’t, at nearly any point, is an effective thriller. The result is diverting straight-to-Netflix fare, sparkly and disposable as a rhinestone, though its star commits as though it were something more.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “there’s no such thing as good girls,” says misty early on in proceedings. It’s not entirely true — the character hides a kind, true heart beneath a gruffly embittered exterior — but it’s a solid pointer for Chastain, always at her most interesting when playing characters who are either morally off-base (“Dreams,” “A Most Violent Year”) or at least a little prickly and defensive. And she comes out, quite literally, all guns blazing: In the film’s opening minutes, she feuds with a neighbor on the remote Georgia pecan farm where she’s settled, eventually taking a shotgun to the woman’s windows. It’s our first taste of the hot temper that cost her a mainstream music career years ago — they called her “the cunt of country,” she says with some relish — though she rarely wields it against someone who doesn’t deserve it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it’s that hard-headed quality that her brother donny (paul sparks) calls upon when he comes to her for help. His 20-something daughter Charlie (singer Carter Faith, in her film debut), herself a buzzy new talent on the Nashville country scene, has recently gone missing, and he suspects shady showbiz machinations at play — something Misty knows plenty about, even if she left that world behind long ago. And so she turns gumshoe, with an oversize felt Stetson instead of a fedora, and a lineup of men to question that range from Charlie’s too-slick-by-half manager Roy (Garrett Hedlund) to an obsessed incel stalker.

Diungkapkan bahwa there are other, hidden reasons for misty to take on a job that isn’t really in her skill set, though they’re not quite satisfyingly addressed, as feste’s script toggles awkwardly between the procedural and the personal. Certain key relationships — notably that between Misty and Donny, brittle with shared secrets — are fleshed out in single scenes, never to be readdressed; elsewhere, the film dawdles on less pivotal connections, though there’s a lovely, wily supporting performance from Sugarland frontwoman Jennifer Nettles as a past friend-turned-rival, culminating in an onstage duet between her and Chastain that’s the highlight of the film’s original and on-the-money country song score. Where characters are sketchily drawn, casting is often more considered: Stalwarts like Hedlund, John Hawkes and Norbert Leo Butz all bring flickers of intelligence and eccentricity to fleeting or one-dimensional roles.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, still, this is chastain’s show, and she’s clearly enjoying it, often daring to play things quite broad and blustery, which rather suits the occasional tackiness of the material; at other points, she convincingly locates a quiet seam of deep-set pain in the protagonist, a casualty of an industry that, it is suggested here, often takes young female talent for a ride. Misty seems vaguely inspired by the enduring mystique of Bobbie Gentry, the prodigious Nashville singer-songwriter who, after a few years at the top, retired from music and checked out of the public eye entirely. Yet the film’s somewhat half-baked mystery tends to distract us from more dramatically probing questions about Misty herself, a curious character in search of a more curious character study.

“Years later, they end up in the same movie,” he enthused.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “the cast always hinged on max’s character, so that’s where we started. Alex Wolff was an immediate choice as not only is he an incredible musician, he can also convey both the world-worn weariness of adulthood and the spark of adolescence, often within the same scene,” he said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “from there, since the story moves fluidly between two timelines without relying on gimmicks, i needed actors who could make the family feel lived-in from the first frame. Jim, with whom I’d worked before, and Sarah possess that warmth and humor, and Brooklynn brings an honesty and maturity that’s rare at any age. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “it’s always hard to put that much of yourself on screen, and there were days on set in ohio that almost felt a little too close to home. Berdasarkan laporan, he added: “making any form of art should always be part exploration and part excavation, and this was the perfect combination of the two. #85. Every SpongeBob SquarePants Christmas & Winter Episode

📅 04 Dec 2020

Every SpongeBob SquarePants Christmas & Winter Episode

Tanggal: 04 Dec 2020 | Sumber: https://screenrant.com/spongebob-squarepants-highest-rated-winter-themed-episodes/

Diungkapkan bahwa spongebob squarepants' christmas episodes show that living in tropical waters isn't a barrier to winter adventures, and the best spongebob christmas episodes also rank among the show's funniest so far. Nickelodeon has consistently delivered some of the best animated TV shows of all time for decades, and, by far, its most popular and successful cartoon is SpongeBob SquarePants. Thanks to its unique characters, setting, fun situations, and different types of comedy, SpongeBob SquarePants has maintained its popularity and relevance for over two decades.

Sebagaimana diketahui, since 1999, spongebob squarepants has taken viewers to the bottom of the ocean, to the town of bikini bottom, to meet the title character and his friends. Throughout 17 seasons, SpongeBob has gotten involved in all types of fun and absurd situations, but living under the sea doesn’t mean that SpongeBob and company don’t get to celebrate the same holidays as those living on land. SpongeBob SquarePants has had various holiday-themed episodes, from Halloween to Christmas and more, but the episodes set in the latter holiday have been the most popular.

Sebagaimana diketahui, while there aren’t many spongebob squarepants episodes dedicated specifically to the spirit of christmas, it does have a few winter-themed stories that fit perfectly with the holiday. Leaving aside the logic and physics of snow underwater, SpongeBob, Patrick, and even Squidward often find their unique brand of festive magic, while sticking to the absurdist humor the show is known for.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "christmas who?" is the first spongebob squarepants christmas special. In it, Sandy is decorating her tree and gearing up for Christmas. SpongeBob and Patrick have never heard of Christmas and learn everything about it from Sandy. SpongeBob does what he does best and gets overexcited and spreads the word around Bikini Bottom.

Diungkapkan bahwa the city becomes a christmas wonderland, but when santa fails to appear on christmas morning, squidward takes it upon himself to become santa and give cheer to bikini bottom. This really shares the meaning of Christmas, with the nice twist that it's Squidward, of all the characters, who gets most into the holiday.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, spongebob and patrick go to sandy's house to play, but find her entire dome covered in a shield with a sign that says "keep out. " The two sneak in to find Sandy asleep, but she doesn't look like herself — she is much larger and fuzzier. Sandy is hibernating for the winter, but SpongeBob and Patrick play in her snow-filled tree dome anyway.

Sebagaimana diketahui, while playing in the snow seems enjoyable and gives this episode a christmas spirit, the noise wakes sandy up, and she’s not pleased. SpongeBob and Patrick end up paying the price for being too loud, and they also begin to struggle with the cold.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "snowball effect" shows bikini bottom under a blanket of snow after an iceberg crashes above. SpongeBob and Patrick spend the episode having a snowball fight, but things take a turn when Squidward gets involved. The three build forts to protect themselves from the snowballs, but Squidward goes too far and realizes he is having more fun than he thought he would.

The snow makes this a Christmas-themed episode, even though it is from an iceberg, but the sight of Squidward playing with SpongeBob and Patrick makes this one of the most enjoyable winter/holiday episodes in the show's history.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "krabs á la mode" shows mr. Krabs turning the Krusty Krab into an unintentional ice rink for winter. Krabs could have done. Due to expenses, Mr. For Squidward, turning down the heat during the frigid temperatures in Bikini Bottom is one of the worst things Mr. Krabs sets an alarm at the Krusty Krab so no one can turn up the heat and turns the Krusty Krab into an ice rink, complete with Krusty Krab-themed skates and activities.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "frozen face-off" celebrates winter with a sled competition, and everyone in bikini bottom enters because the prize is $1 million. SpongeBob has Gary leading his sled, Patrick chooses gummy worms to take him to victory, and Squidward has a worm who chooses to sip tea instead of winning the race.

Sebagaimana diketahui, while everyone tries to win the prize, plankton is busy trying to steal the krabby patty secret recipe. When the gang tries to stop him, they're frozen in ice, but the ever-resourceful Sandy makes a fire to warm everyone up, ending the episode on a festively-themed note of the value of friendship and cooperation.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "it's a spongebob christmas" is, arguably, the best spongebob christmas episode. To celebrate the holidays, this episode shows Bikini Bottom excited about Santa's arrival. As always, Plankton has an evil plan up his sleeve to ruin Christmas cheer, so he puts all of Bikini Bottom on Santa's naughty list.

Sebagaimana diketahui, what makes this episode stand out is the fact that it’s not traditionally animated like other spongebob squarepants christmas episodes. Instead, the episode is animated in claymation and pays homage to Christmas claymation classics.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in this episode, squidward tries to sell his art at the krusty krab, but when mr. Krabs shuts it down, he sends Squidward to Antarctica to bring his art to a big-time buyer. Once there, Squidward comes across a snow sponge that looks a lot like a snowman.

Berdasarkan laporan, as it turns out, spongebob is (somehow) already in antarctica eating ice by the time squidward gets there. This episode brings Squidward and SpongeBob to a snowy terrain that is unlike what they normally experience in Bikini Bottom, with the change of locale being a clever way to tap into the Christmas themes.

Diungkapkan bahwa "shopping list" doesn't include santa or snowball fights, but it does include a cold-living yeti. Krabs gives SpongeBob an intense shopping list with odd things that aren't easily found. In the episode, Mr. Sandy decides to help SpongeBob since she is braver than him, especially when it comes to getting the hair of a Yeti.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, sandy and spongebob get the job done, but the yeti eventually tracks them down to get its hair back. It offers a small touch of winter magic that enters Bikini Bottom, along with one of winter's most mythical creatures.

Berdasarkan laporan, “goons on the moon” sees sandy taking her science scout troop on a trip to the moon. #90. ‘Law & Order: SVU’ Goes Back to (Before) the Beginning With Its 600th Episode

‘Law & Order: SVU’ Goes Back to (Before) the Beginning With Its 600th Episode

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/law-and-order-svu-600th-episode-showrunner-interview-1236754391/

Showrunner Michele Fazekas breaks down Christopher Meloni's return and the state of the Benson-Stabler relationship.

Diungkapkan bahwa [this story contains spoilers from the 600th episode of law & order: svu. ].

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, law & order: svu reached a huge milestone thursday: 600 episodes, a number that only two scripted primetime shows have ever hit before. The cast and crew celebrated with a cake on set during filming and a dinner afterward — and then went back to work. Six hundred episodes is an extremely rare feat for a scripted series (The Simpsons and Gunsmoke are the only ones with more), but Thursday’s episode was also the sixth of season 28; 15 more are still to come. Related Stories Business Fanatics Studios' Next Big Media Play Is the NBA All-Star Game TV Jason Benetti Will Replace Dan Hicks on Notre Dame Play-by-Play Saturday Following Sudden Passing (Exclusive).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “that’s just doing television,” showrunner michele fazekas told the hollywood reporter. “It’s our 600th episode, but it’s also just an episode within 21 episodes [this season]. You’re working on five episodes at the same time at any given moment — you’re in prep on some episodes, you’re writing on some episodes, you’re in post on some episodes. Nothing changed in that regard. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa titled “obedience,” the 600th episode brings elliot stabler (christopher meloni) back to the special victims unit after jury consultant gwen sharpe (j. Smith-Cameron, who also appeared in the season premiere) convinces Benson (Mariska Hargitay) to take another look at an old case. Gwen is convinced the man in prison for the crime, the rape and murder of a young nun in 1998, is innocent.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, stabler is reluctant to revisit the case — with good reason, it turns out. He failed to follow a couple of leads that could have pointed to the real culprit, a now-retired priest who led mass at the convent where the victim lived. He also cut Benson out of the interrogation in the case, which she went along with at the time because she was new to the squad. The case stirs up complicated feelings in the former partners; when Stabler asks Benson why she’s so interested in digging up the case, she retorts, “Why aren’t you?”.

He eventually agrees to work with her, and the pair head upstate to question people who knew the victim (most notably, guest stars Laura Innes and Kathleen Chalfant) and track down the priest.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, fazekas, who wrote the episode (brenna malloy directed), said she wanted to give the 600th show the feel of “an old school benson and stabler episode” while also looking at the people they have become in the years since. To that end, the episode’s final scenes will give viewers plenty to discuss.

Fazekas unpacked those scenes, the reasons for going back to the show’s early days and more in an interview with THR.

Given the milestone that this is, was there extra planning that went into it? Or did you have ideas on the board for longer than you might normally?.

Berdasarkan laporan, probably a little bit. I think I had an idea early on in the in the season of what I wished to do, and one of the first things was saying, “Can we bring back Chris Meloni?” Assuming that this is the last centennial episode that we were going to have, it feels like if we could do it, this would be the time to do it. So yeah, there were some earlier ideas than your typical running around trying to figure out what an episode is.

Having Stabler come back into the squad was always part of the plan, then?.

Diungkapkan bahwa it was for me. ” I want them to be in a car, driving long distances and hashing stuff out. I just had an idea, and I don’t usually come up with ideas this way, but I was like, “I want it to be a road show. I didn’t know what [the reason] was. There were a lot of things that had to happen in order for that to become a reality, including Chris having to be available — he’s busy. But he was. I also knew early on — because I was on the show the first time around, seasons three through seven — I wanted to kind of go back a little bit to an old school Benson and Stabler episode of SVU and honor that era of the show. I always find that interesting, just putting two people in a place where they can’t get away, and then they have to hash out their stuff.

Berdasarkan laporan, the structure of svu is such that cases usually get cleared and some sort of justice is served by the end of the hour. I thought it was really interesting that this one is built on something that they got wrong initially. Why did you want to come at it that way?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in part, it was because you have to explain why are we bringing detective stabler back. He works in a completely different department. So what would be big enough that he would come back? It felt sort of organic for it to be an old case, but it’s a case that actually predates the show. He doesn’t work in SVU anymore. The show starts in 1999, and this case is from 1998.

Sebagaimana diketahui, what was not planned but came out in the in the breaking of the story is they were such different people back then. Benson was really new, and Stabler was the senior detective, and she has evolved so much because, at the end of the day, we’re still telling the story of Benson. It fits really nicely into what we’re doing with her character this season, and it made sense for why he’s back. But it also goes to wanting to do and old school SVU episodes, but let’s go back to before SVU was even a thing.

Berdasarkan laporan, i was also struck by stabler admitting to benson that his catholicism might have blinded him to who the real perpetrator was. His religion has been a thread throughout the character’s run, but I think it’s always interesting when it comes up explicitly in relation to a case.

Diungkapkan bahwa chris meloni was a big proponent of that as well. Anybody who was raised Catholic, you think of it as one thing, and it’s very hard for people to accept that this thing that you think is one way has a really dark side. I think allowing your own preconceptions biases you; it goes to that whole issue [of blind spots] generally. At that time [in 1998], it would have been really hard for Stabler to even understand.

Diungkapkan bahwa you were on the show for a good portion of the benson-stabler partnership during your first tenure, and now you’re back as showrunner. What’s your read on their relationship?.

Diungkapkan bahwa my read is stabler still has work to do on himself that benson has done. Benson has evolved in a way, and I love them together, and I love them as partners and as scene partners. I think Stabler is still working on it. But I think part of this episode is talking about how she, in some ways, has moved on from the struggles back then. Stabler is still doing a lot of the same things that he did 20 years ago, and he’s starting to realize, oh, I need to change that.

And given what goes on between them in this episode — arguing about work and life, and then him inviting her to come to Arizona for a while — what do you think the audience’s read is going to be?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, listen, i do think they love each other. I don’t think he didn’t mean it, but he also knew what her answer was going to be, and I think now is not the time. It’s easy to ask that question when you know the answer is no. I think they both know. I think when he says, “Hey, you want to come to Arizona?” he knows her answer is going to be no. Is there time down the line? Maybe, but I think he’s got some work to do. She can have some work to do as well, but I think she’s probably a little further down that path than he is.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i’ve always thought that they love each other in a way that sort of transcends a sexual relationship. They deeply love each other, and they’ve acknowledged that before, and I think this sort of reinforces it. But I also think he knows I’ve got more to do with myself.

Where are you in terms of production now?.

We are shooting episode 10 and in prep on episode 11.

Anything you can say about the next few episodes?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we have a nice little arc going of that we started at the beginning of the season that we continue, where the cases that they’re faced with are messy and don’t have easy answers. No matter how hard we work, sometimes it doesn’t matter. Benson is really struggling with feeling like nothing has changed. I like the idea of pushing her — the episode we’re shooting now and the next episode are pushing her to the edges of not even what is legal, but what is ethically and morally right to do, because she’s starting to not care.

Diungkapkan bahwa the episode we’re shooting right now, the bad guy is so bad. We’re talking about “Why is he doing what he’s doing?” And she actually says, “I don’t care,” which is a big thing for her. But you also understand it because the guy is such a bad guy.

Anything you can say about how Stephanie March re-enters the show as Alex Cabot?.

Diungkapkan bahwa benson goes to her and asks for help. They didn’t end things on a totally happy note the last time she was on the show, but Benson goes back to her.

Is Alex still doing the same sort of work she was that last time?.

#96. Why Quentin Tarantino Initially Fired Mélanie Laurent and Isabelle Huppert From ‘Inglourious Basterds’

📅 13 Nov 2026

Why Quentin Tarantino Initially Fired Mélanie Laurent and Isabelle Huppert From ‘Inglourious Basterds’

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/quentin-tarantino-fired-melanie-laurent-isabelle-huppert-inglourious-basterds-1236754336/

Sebagaimana diketahui, "if it’s not right, it is not right. I owe my film the best actors I can find. I don’t owe them sh**. Period," the Oscar-winning filmmaker said in Jay Glennie’s new book.

Quentin Tarantino is getting candid about his decision to fire Mélanie Laurent and Isabelle Huppert before production began for 2009’s Inglourious Basterds.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the oscar-winning filmmaker opened up in jay glennie’s new book, the making of quentin tarantino’s inglourious basterds, about why he feels he doesn’t owe actors “shit,” but owes “my film the best actors i can find. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the dark comedy war film, set in nazi-occupied france during world war ii, centers on a plan to assassinate nazi leaders by a group of jewish u. soldiers. However, the plan ends up coinciding with a theatre owner’s vengeful plans to do the same. S. Related Stories Exclusive Excerpt Brad Pitt, Tarantino and a Bong Full of Hash: The Untold Origin Story of 'Inglourious Basterds' Movies Cinemark Won't Screen Brad Pitt's 'Cliff Booth' Movie Over Netflix's Demands, CEO Says.

Though Laurent was eventually rehired for the leading role of Shosanna Dreyfus, the French cinema owner, Tarantino said her initial “table read was terrible,” so he let her go.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “it wasn’t good enough to be terrible,” tarantino told glennie. “The most exciting day of preproduction is for me the table read. Up until then, it’s just been me reading all the scenes to myself or to a friend … so a table read with the whole cast is so exciting and so important to me. That is the closest I get to seeing the movie for the first time. Well, Mélanie was terrible, so I fired her. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, tarantino recalled laurent calling him to get her job back, explaining she was feeling under the weather at the time of the table read. A persistent Laurent also planned to show up to set regardless of his decision. “I will fly myself to Germany and put myself up into a hotel. I know you’re busy, but I will wait until you see me again,” she told the filmmaker.

Sebagaimana diketahui, she eventually convinced tarantino to give her another chance, saying he would “turn the clock back” and “they would return to square one. ” However, he wouldn’t fully decide if “she was his Shosanna Dreyfus” until after three days of rehearsal.

Diungkapkan bahwa laurent ultimately won over tarantino, going on to play the lead role. “Let me just go on the record for everybody to know: I love Mélanie,” the director told the author.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “the fact of the matter is, if we were not talking about the making of inglourious basterds, i would never think about the table read again for the simple reason mélanie is my shosanna,” he added. You know, we agreed, warts and all. But we have decided to dive deep into the making of the movie with this book, and this is an important part of its history. “She did a wonderful job. So, if we had not agreed to talk about the shooting of the movie, it would be out of my mind, and I would never think about it again. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa huppert was a bit of a different story. After being cast as Madame Ada Mimieux, a woman who provides shelter to Shosanna in Paris, Tarantino fired her when she didn’t show up for the table read.

Diungkapkan bahwa “she didn’t show up, so fuck it. I fired her,” he said. Well, we cast Maggie Cheung instead. It just kept stalling. “I mean, I love Isabelle Huppert — Heaven’s Gate and all that — but there were issues with her contract. And then not coming to the table read. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “that invariably happens. As far as I’m concerned, if you’re cast and you are not at that table, I don’t owe you jack shit! You can be fired, especially if I get excited by what somebody else did in your absence,” Tarantino continued. He used Michael Parks being cast in two different roles in his Kill Bill films, replacing Ricardo Montalbán, as another example.

Despite Cheung taking on the role, Tarantino ultimately decided to cut those scenes with her character from the movie.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “maggie was fantastic in the movie, but you just didn’t need to know how shosanna acquired the cinema. All we needed was a title card saying Four Years Later and Shosanna explaining that she inherited it from her aunt,” Tarantino explained.

Berdasarkan laporan, following its release in 2009, inglourious basterds went on to gross more than $321 million worldwide. It also earned eight Academy Award nominations, with Christoph Waltz taking home the best supporting actor Oscar for his role as Col. Hans Landa.

Diungkapkan bahwa “i have no moral compass when it comes to giving roles to actors: they have to be right. If it’s not right, it is not right. Period. “I have fired actors in the past. They have to feel like they are right for the world I have created,” Tarantino told Glennie about his approach to casting actors. I don’t owe them shit. I owe my film the best actors I can find. ”.

#97. Latin Grammys 2026 Winners: The Complete List

📅 13 Nov 2026

Latin Grammys 2026 Winners: The Complete List

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-latin/latin-grammys-2026-winners-complete-list-1235655791/

On Thursday night, Latin music’s biggest stars took over Las Vegas’ MGM Grand Garden Arena for the Latin Grammys, celebrating the best of 2026.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it’s no surprise that rosalía made latin grammys history when she took home her third album of the year award after a night of several wins. Before she opened the ceremony with operatic flair, the Spanish superstar took home four trophies: Best Alternative Album for her showstopping album Lux, Best Pop Song for highlight “La Perla,” and Best Short Form Music Video for “Sauvignon Blanc. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “the truth is i know i have a lot to learn. I know that I’ve probably made my best work but I know there’s still a lot left to be the best,” Rosalía said in her AOTY acceptance speech. I don’t know if another one is going to fit in your house, but I’ll bring it to you anyways and see if you make room. “Thanks, mama, for making me this way. I’m going to bring this Grammy to your house. You always find a way for anything,” she added.

Berdasarkan laporan, in another emotional highlight, karol g took home best urban music album for her 2025 lp, tropicoqueta after being award best reggaeton performance before the ceremony. “I’m going to very honest because God willing I’ve been up here a couple of times but this one is special,” the Colombian superstar said in her acceptance speech. “People always hear the end result but making Tropicoqueta meant a lot to me that people can’t even imagine. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa karol continued: “the most important part is to have an album that i can tour because i feel when i’m singing it, people feel proud to be latina and to carry their flags with pride. That’s the most beautiful part. ” Before she walked off, Karol let out an impassioned yell: “Latina forever!”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, milo j had a big night as well, earning his first latin grammys ever and eventually walking home with four awards total. The 20 year-old Argentine musician nabbed Song of the Year for his track “Solifican12” and Best Folk Album for La Vida Era Más Corta.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, argentine duo ca7riel and paco amoroso were early winners of the night, nabbing awards for “best electronic music performance” and “best pop/rock song. and Sting become first-time Latin Grammy winners. ” With their wins, they helped both Fred Again. #101. The 6 Most Hopeless Thriller TV Shows, Ranked

📅 13 Nov 2026

The 6 Most Hopeless Thriller TV Shows, Ranked

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://collider.com/most-hopeless-thriller-tv-shows-ranked/

Diungkapkan bahwa feel free to connect with him or check out his work. He's everywhere — Upwork, YouTube, Spotify, SoundCloud, Collider, LinkedIn, Instagram.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a hopeless thriller is one that keeps you grabbed by the neck but still ends in a painful manner. Surviving what it does to your life is another. It's heartbreaking. Someone in a thriller says, “We just need to find the truth,” and I immediately start worrying about them. Because finding the truth is one thing. It's infuriating. I've watched characters sacrifice everything to uncover a secret, only to discover that knowing the answer doesn't give them the slightest power to change it. And when a show earns that feeling, I cannot look away.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i think helplessness becomes truly frightening when you can understand every decision that leads somebody there. You wouldn't necessarily have behaved differently. You might have trusted the same person, followed the same evidence, or convinced yourself that one more sacrifice would finally put things right. These six thrillers are merciless about that very human tendency.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, sarah linden (mireille enos) is preparing to leave the seattle police department when the disappearance of teenager rosie larsen interrupts her plans. She works alongside detective Stephen Holder (Joel Kinnaman) and investigates a murder that tears through Rosie's family and becomes entangled with a political campaign. The Killing makes the investigation painfully personal, particularly for Rosie's parents, Stan (Brent Sexton) and Mitch (Michelle Forbes).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, what gets under my skin is how little the truth can actually repair. Meanwhile, Linden's inability to abandon the case damages her relationship with her own son. Stan's grief keeps twisting into anger, leaving him vulnerable to decisions that could destroy what's left of his family. Everybody wants justice, but nobody can promise that justice will make living any easier. Mitch can barely function inside the home where her daughter should still be living. I find that distinction absolutely devastating.

Berdasarkan laporan, paul spector (jamie dornan) has a wife, children, and a job as a grief counselor. He also stalks and murders women in Belfast. The Fall makes no secret of the murderer's identity. Detective Superintendent Stella Gibson (Gillian Anderson) arrives to investigate the killings, gradually closing in on a man who appears disturbingly ordinary outside his crimes. We know who he is, and the awful suspense comes from watching him move through a city full of people who don't.

Sebagaimana diketahui, dornan's most disturbing moments aren't necessarily the violent ones. His domestic life offers camouflage without making his affection straightforwardly false, which is a sickening contradiction. Gibson is formidable, but intelligence and determination cannot undo what his victims have experienced. Sometimes Paul is simply behaving affectionately toward his children, and I want him as far away from them as possible. Even catching him means confronting the lasting damage he's inflicted. This is a thriller where the prospect of victory never feels remotely satisfying enough.

Sebagaimana diketahui, mr. Elliot Alderson (Rami Malek) works in cybersecurity while secretly hacking people and organizations he believes deserve exposing. Robot (Christian Slater) recruits him into a movement determined to destroy the financial power of E Corp, Elliot sees an opportunity to strike back at a system he despises. When the mysterious Mr. Robot begins with a thrilling fantasy of rebellion. The movie gradually questions whether Elliot understands the consequences of his own actions.

Berdasarkan laporan, i remember being almost embarrassingly excited about fsociety's ambitions. Sam Esmail, the show's creator, pushes that contradiction to its most painful extreme during Elliot's conversations with therapist Krista. But Elliot's loneliness is even harder to endure. Then the economic damage starts spreading, ordinary people suffer, and the promised revolution becomes another nightmare. The man determined to expose the world's hidden cruelty has spent years struggling to confront his own suffering. He can access almost anybody's private information while remaining terrified of genuine human intimacy. There is compassion here, thankfully, but very little comes without a terrible emotional cost.

Sebagaimana diketahui, will graham (hugh dancy) possesses a remarkable ability to understand how murderers think, making him invaluable to fbi investigator jack crawford (laurence fishburne). Hannibal Lecter (Mads Mikkelsen), an extraordinarily sophisticated psychiatrist who happens to be a cannibalistic serial killer. His increasingly fragile mental state leads him into therapy with Dr. Hannibal transforms their relationship into a psychological battle where affection, manipulation, and violence become almost impossible to separate.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i've never hated a fictional friendship quite so passionately. That attention feels almost loving, even as Hannibal deliberately destabilizes the person receiving it. Mikkelsen can turn a quiet dinner invitation into something sinister, while Dancy makes Will's desperate need for connection painfully convincing. Hannibal recognizes Will's loneliness and offers him the intoxicating possibility of being completely understood. The second season's confrontation at Hannibal's home is among the cruelest emotional disasters I've watched on television. What destroys me is that neither man can simply dismiss their attachment afterward. Understanding one another has become another form of imprisonment.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, four criminal masterminds. One of them was always going to be yours. Here is who comes for you, why they picked you out of everyone available, and what they want from the encounter.

Sebagaimana diketahui, your nemesis does not want to beat you. He wants to know you completely, and he is patient enough to wait for it. The frightening part is how good the conversation is.

Diungkapkan bahwa your nemesis is not after money, territory or revenge. He is after a demonstration, and you are the person he has chosen to prove his point on.

Sebagaimana diketahui, your nemesis respects you, which sounds flattering until you work out what it means. He chose you because nobody else was worth his time.

Berdasarkan laporan, your nemesis has no personal interest in you whatsoever, and that is precisely what makes him unsurvivable. You are not a rival. You are a stop on the way.

Diungkapkan bahwa a mysterious graphic novel called the utopia experiments draws a group of internet acquaintances into a conspiracy involving a ruthless organization known as the network. Ian (Nathan Stewart-Jarrett), Becky (Alexandra Roach), Wilson Wilson (Adeel Akhtar), and young Grant (Oliver Woollford) find themselves pursued by killers who will do practically anything to obtain the manuscript. The original British Utopia turns their attempts to survive into an increasingly terrifying struggle against an organization whose influence seems limitless.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “where is jessica hyde?” i swear, those four words become enough to make me nervous. Survival gradually demands compromises that make the protagonists resemble the people they're fighting. The show was canceled after two seasons, leaving its extraordinary atmosphere of dread hanging over an unfinished story. Arby (Neil Maskell) asks the question with horrifying calm, as though killing people is simply an inconvenient part of his workday. The Network's resources are staggering, but the truly sickening part is its conviction that committing atrocities can be justified as serving humanity's future. Dennis Kelly's writing refuses to offer the comfort of uncomplicated heroes either. Somehow, that feels appropriately cruel.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a young boy disappears in the german town of winden, leading several families toward a mystery involving a network of caves, disturbing family secrets, and events separated by decades. Jonas Kahnwald (Louis Hofmann) becomes central to the investigation as Dark gradually establishes a world where time travel connects generations of people who barely understand the consequences of their own decisions.

Berdasarkan laporan, ulrich nielsen (oliver masucci) is the character who really breaks my heart. Lovers become trapped by histories they don't understand. Watching that certainty turn into something terrible is almost unbearable. And the cruelest part is that I never stop hoping alongside them. Creators Baran bo Odar and Jantje Friese construct a world where love repeatedly becomes the reason people perpetuate suffering. His desperation to find his missing son pushes him toward an act he believes could prevent decades of suffering. I want Ulrich to find his family. Parents damage children they haven't met yet. But the show's bleakest idea extends far beyond one father's mistake. I want Jonas to save Martha. Attempts to prevent catastrophes can help bring them about. I want somebody, anybody, to escape the terrible inheritance passed between generations.

#104. Stacy Keach Played A Villain In One Of The Best Batman Movies Of All Time

📅 13 Nov 2026

Stacy Keach Played A Villain In One Of The Best Batman Movies Of All Time

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.slashfilm.com/2315598/stacy-keach-batman-mask-of-the-phantasm-villain-role-explained/

Sebagaimana diketahui, actor stacy keach passed away on november 10, 2026, leaving behind a huge list of film, television, and theatre credits across his lifetime. Typecasting never really caught up with Keach. He could play diametrically different characters, like how he acted as both the morally upright Warden Henry Pope in "Prison Break" and Neo-Nazi leader Cameron Alexander in "American History X. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, even so, keach's deep voice often coded him as a tough guy you don't want to mess with. DC Comics and Batman fans will recognize that voice from "Batman: Mask of the Phantasm," one of the best Batman movies, animated or otherwise. The titular villain is a skull-masked, scythe-wielding vigilante targeting gangsters in Gotham City. Unlike Batman (Kevin Conroy), the Phantasm employs lethal force.

Sebagaimana diketahui, keach voices the phantasm (at least when they're wearing their mask). The Phantasm doesn't say that much, admittedly, because silence serves their menacing presence more. But whenever the Phantasm first appears in a plume of smoke, they announce themselves with this line: "[Name], your angel of death awaits!" Keach makes the Phantasm's voice live up to those words. It's deep and ghostly, with an echo that sounds like he is genuinely an apparition from beyond the mortal plane.

Diungkapkan bahwa "mask of the phantasm" features a dual timeline structure; half of the movie takes place in bruce wayne's youth before he becomes batman. Keach has a second role in this storyline as Carl Beaumont, Andrea's financier father. He romances Andrea Beaumont (Dana Delany), the woman he almost chose over becoming Batman. Naturally, you then make the leap (subconsciously or not) in thinking that Carl is the Phantasm, especially once we learn he was once indebted to the gangsters the Phantasm is killing in the present. That's just what the movie wants you to think.

Berdasarkan laporan, okay, enough hiding behind spoilers: the phantasm is actually andrea herself. But the gangsters caught up to the Beaumonts, killed Carl, and now Andrea is back for revenge. (Amusingly, the twist of Andrea being the Phantasm was spoiled by some tie-in toys. She and her father had to flee the country to dodge his loan shark debtors, which is why she canceled her engagement to Bruce all those years ago. ).

Diungkapkan bahwa keach's part as carl gets back to his acting range. Diegetically, Andrea has given her alter ego her father's voice to throw suspicion off herself. The red herring of Carl being the Phantasm becomes text late in the movie, after Andrea and Bruce rekindle their relationship and she explains why she left him — except for the part that her dad is dead. He plays, essentially, the Grim Reaper and a terrified father, and he's great in both parts. While framing her father might dishonor his memory, she's also playing the part of Carl Beaumont's vengeful spirit to kill his killers.

Diungkapkan bahwa batman having a romantic connection with a foe is nothing new — just ask catwoman or talia al ghul. "Mask of the Phantasm" commits to being a romantic tragedy; Batman doesn't reach or redeem Andrea, who chooses her vengeance. The Phantasm's backstory has the foundation for a redemption, but happy endings are hard to come by in Gotham City. The final two scenes of the film show Andrea and then Bruce, both alone again. But at least Batman still has Gotham.

Berdasarkan laporan, "mask of the phantasm" remains widely beloved and is often considered the late kevin conroy's greatest performance as batman. Stacy Keach as the Phantasm was an essential ingredient, too, and may he also rest in peace.

#109. Universal's Best Twilight / Harry Potter Replacement Has Been In Development Hell For Six Years

📅 13 Nov 2026

Universal's Best Twilight / Harry Potter Replacement Has Been In Development Hell For Six Years

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://screenrant.com/crave-harry-potter-twilight-replacement-development-hell/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, step aside, twilight, and move over, harry potter; universal has the perfect answer to both. It may seem an unlikely combination; Twilight is a "sparkly vampire" romance, while Harry Potter blazed the trail for the current generation of magic schools (complete with a healthy dose of a Chosen One destiny). And yet, have you ever noticed how the best original stories are a delightful mix of multiple ideas, creating something refreshingly new and yet delightfully familiar?.

Berdasarkan laporan, step forward tracy wolff's crave, which is a stunning blend of the two. It stars Grace Foster, a young orphan who winds up sent to what turns out to be a school for vampires, werewolves, dragons, witches, and more. And, of course, the different groups don't get on at all. The book is delightfully self-aware (at one point the vampire love-interest gives Grace a gift copy of Twilight), and it turns so many of the central tropes upside-down in a fantastic way.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, crave launched in 2020, and it's expanded into a full six-book series. Katmere Academy isn't Hogwarts; it's much more dangerous, a little closer to the dark academia books I've fallen in love with of late. The various factions initially feel almost like your traditional high school, where the jocks and the nerds all hang out together, but it soon becomes clear the racial "tribes" are much more dangerous. Grace has no idea what she's dealing with, and initially there's an entertaining sense of denial as readers figure out what's happening even as she tries to tell herself she's going nuts.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that said, my personal favorite twist here is that the heroes are not the chosen ones. In fact, this is a franchise where the Chosen One went wrong; where the vampire love interest's brother was believed to be a Chosen One, and was raised to believe he was something special. It's fascinating to realize how much this kind of philosophy can twist and scar a person, making the Crave story a fun interrogation of a trope we've seen played out so many times. It reminds me a little of Anakin Skywalker in the Star Wars prequels, but a little better done (with apologies to George Lucas).

Berdasarkan laporan, as a lover of twilight and harry potter, and someone who very much enjoys romantasy, i can honestly say crave is a must-read. Wolff is wonderfully creative, and her world is so very immersive; even when she plays with familiar tropes and character beats, she does so with a nod and a wink. If you like vampires and werewolves, magic schools, or even dragon shifters, this is the series for you.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but here's the annoying thing; universal acquired the rights to crave before the first book even came out, with universal’s svp of production jeyun munford and creative executive christine sun set to oversee the production. We've had zero news about the film since then, though, which is something of a surprise; unfortunately, Munford isn't even at Universal anymore, which may well mean this particular movie has been lost in development hell. If so, it's a real shame; at a time when both Harry Potter and Twilight are re-emerging, this is an epic that should really be given a chance to flourish.

For now, readers would be wise to pick up Crave for something that will definitely scratch that itch in the best possible way.
